text.p: Earnings forecasts for Italy's automotive and industrial group Fiat SpA have been downgraded for 1996 and 1997 by investment bank CS First Boston due to a depressed Italian car market and the stronger lira.
In a research note, CSFB said it is cutting its 1996 earnings forecast to 264 lire/share from 379 lire, and for 1997 down to 312 lire/share from 441 lire.

"The potential for earnings growth in 1997 depends crucially, in our view, on the development of Italian demand and there appears to be, as yet, no signs of more buoyant consumer demand," said CSFB analyst Susanne Oliver in the note.

CSFB points out that Fiat is expected to release 9-month 1996 turnover figures after a board meeting today, with CSFB looking for a five percent rise to 58.80 trillion lire. Fiat may also release a profit figure and CSFB is looking for a pretax profit of 1.7-1.8 trillion with no comparison available.
In the first half of 1996, Fiat made a pretax of 1.547 trillion lire.

CSFB pointed out that its forecast downgrades reflect two main factors. First, an expensive rebate programme in Fiat's domestic market and Fiat's recent loss of market share, and second, the strength of the Italian lira.

The investment bank pointed out that there are two bright spots for Fiat -- gains in market share in Europe outside Italy, and the success of the Palio model in Brazil. But these were not enough to offset the negative factors, it added.
